Issues.Title: fix(http): clean up pending tasks when interceptors throw synchronously
Issues.Body:
## Description

When an HTTP interceptor throws synchronously during chain execution, the pending task added by `HttpInterceptorHandler` was never cleaned up because `.pipe(finalize(removeTask))` was never attached to an Observable stream. This caused `ApplicationRef.whenStable()` to hang.

This PR addresses the issue by:
1. Wrapping chain execution in `try ... catch` within `HttpInterceptorHandler` to ensure `removeTask()` is called if an interceptor throws synchronously before rethrowing the error.
2. Removing redundant `PendingTasks` tracking from `legacyInterceptorFnFactory`. `HttpInterceptorHandler` already manages the pending task for the entire request, so tracking it again inside the legacy adapter was duplicating pending tasks for every request using `withInterceptorsFromDi()`.
3. Adding regression tests verifying application stability after synchronous interceptor errors for both functional and legacy interceptors.

Closes #71953

Issues.Title: fix(core): suppress hydration warnings in test environments
Issues.Body:
When running component tests in TestBed, an application configuration may include `provideClientHydration()` (e.g. from `appConfig.providers`) or use `@defer` blocks with `hydrate` triggers without hydration providers configured.

In these testing scenarios, there is no serialized server state in `TransferState` because the tests run purely in the test runner. As a result, Angular emitted spurious warnings:
- `NG0505`: warning that client hydration was requested on the client, but no serialized information was present in the server response.
- `NG0508`: warning that incremental hydration is not enabled when `@defer (hydrate ...)` triggers are used.

This commit introduces an internal `IS_TESTING` token (defaulting to `false`), which is provided as `true` by `TestBedCompiler` and `BrowserTestingModule`. It suppresses both warnings when running inside a testing environment.

Fixes #62053

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): reduce preprocessor incremental fingerprinting overhead
Issues.Body:
This change reduces JS serialization and hashing overhead during incremental `HybridCompiler` runs.

When compiling components with large dependency metadata, `HybridCompiler.computeBoundFingerprint` previously ran `JSON.stringify` and JS string hashing over the full `AnalysisResult` (including `resolvedDeclarations`), and computed that fingerprint twice per component file across `prepareChunk` and `processFile`.

What changed:
- Derive `Hash` on `AnalysisResult` and its nested wire structs in Rust `ng-analyze` (switching `deferredImports` block maps from `HashMap` to `BTreeMap` for deterministic ordering) and attach a `DefaultHasher` digest as an optional `fingerprint` field during `FileData::to_wire`. `HybridCompiler.computeBoundFingerprint` uses that digest rather than serializing large `AnalysisResult` objects in JS, and `remoteScopeInputs` skips serializing `eagerlyUsedDeclarations` for classes that are not remotely scoped.
- Record `analysisResult` on `FileAnalysis` during template binding in `prepareFileAnalysisForBinding` and `populateBoundData`, and reuse `FileAnalysis.boundFingerprint` in `processFile` when `analysisResult`, `sourceContent`, and `boundFingerprint` match.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): reduce preprocessor incremental fingerprinting overhead" (#71976)

Issues.Title: fix(devtools): stop zoom transition when disposing the tree visualizer
Issues.Body:
## What is the current behavior?

Snapping to a node in the tree visualizer starts a 500ms d3 zoom transition that is not interrupted on `dispose()`. If the visualizer is destroyed mid-transition, d3-zoom keeps reading the size of the detached SVG and throws:

```
NotSupportedError: Failed to read the 'value' property from 'SVGLength'
```

The router tree spec ran with `provideZoneChangeDetection()` (with a TODO to migrate), and its single `fixture.detectChanges()` never ran the visualizer's render effect, so the tree was never drawn and this path was not covered.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Two commits:

1. `fix(devtools)`: interrupt any running transition in `TreeVisualizer.dispose()`.
2. `refactor(devtools)`: run the router tree spec zoneless (remove `provideZoneChangeDetection()` and the TODO, replace `fixture.detectChanges()` with `await fixture.whenStable()`). The tree is now rendered and snapped to the root, which fails with the error above without the first commit.

Issues.Title: feat(core): resolve element attributes with attribute resolvers
Issues.Body:
Proposal: angular/angular#67519 When a component, its other directives, and the template all set one attribute on an element, Angular keeps whichever write comes last: a directive's `[attr.role]` overwrites the template's static `role`, and conflicting utility classes such as `px-4` and `px-2` both stay. This PR lets an app decide: a resolver binding, `(attr.x)`, or the `(class)` and `(style)` shorthands, receives every source of the attribute in priority order and resolves them into one value, with a resolver that the app provides per attribute name.
What it looks like ```ts bootstrapApplication(App, { providers: [provideAttributeResolvers({class: twMerge, 'aria-describedby': joinTokens})], }); @Component({ selector: 'ui-button', host: {class: 'inline-flex h-9 px-4 bg-primary', '(class)': 'classes'}, template: '', }) export class UiButton { readonly disabled = input(false); protected readonly classes: ClassCallback = (cn) => cn(this.disabled() && 'bg-muted'); } ``` ```html
  • ``` With `withAutoResolution()` in the root providers, every element that a component or directive matches resolves its enrolled attributes without a binding.
    How it runs ```text refreshView _refreshAttributeResolvers(lView) # null unless an app uses the feature for each resolved attribute of an element collect sources # [component, directives, template], per grammar for each resolver binding, lowest priority first handler($event) # ClassResolveEvent | StyleResolveEvent | AttributeResolveEvent $event.resolver(...extras) # the app's resolver for this name, or the built-in rule $event.resolve(value) fold the result into the sources for the next binding apply # class: diff; style: per-property diff; others: one write ``` Four grammars decide how sources are read and applied: class lists (`class`), declarations (`style`), token lists (`rel`, `aria-describedby`, and similar), and scalars (every other name). Built-in rules: `lastValue`, `joinTokens`, `joinDeclarations`, and `joinValues(separator)`. Attributes whose value needs sanitization (`href`, `src` on most elements, `on*`, namespaced names) can't be resolved: a compile error in templates and host bindings, and skipped per element by automatic resolution.
    New public API (`@angular/core`, all `@experimental 22.3`) - `provideAttributeResolvers(resolvers, ...features)`, `withAutoResolution(enabled?)` - `lastValue`, `joinTokens`, `joinDeclarations`, `joinValues` - `AttributeResolver`, `ClassResolver`, `AttributeResolverFeature` - `AttributeResolveEvent`, `ClassResolveEvent`, `StyleResolveEvent`, `AttributeSources`, `ClassSources`, `ResolvedAttribute` - `AttributeValue`, `ClassBindingValue`, `StyleBindingValue`, `BoundClassResolver`, `BoundStyleResolver`, `ClassCallback`, `StyleCallback` Runtime codes `NG0320`–`NG0324`; compiler codes `NG8120` (`outputShadowedByAttributeResolver`), `NG8121`, and `NG8122` (`propertyBindingBypassesResolver`).
    Commits: review one at a time; before the rebase onto the current main, each built and passed its own targets 1. `feat(core): add an attribute resolver runtime`: the instruction, per-element data, the class, token-list, and scalar grammars, `provideAttributeResolvers`, the hooks. Nothing emits the instruction yet; its direct API specs run in a core-only target. 2. `feat(compiler): compile attribute resolver bindings`: the classifier, the template pipeline and i18n lowering, the host security exclusion, the `22.3.0` partial `minVersion`, the acceptance and SSR specs. `BREAKING CHANGE` for listeners named `class` and `attr.x`. 3. `feat(compiler-cli): validate attribute resolver host bindings`: the host declaration rules and the `@HostListener` errors. `BREAKING CHANGE` for `@HostListener`. 4. `feat(compiler-cli): type-check attribute resolver bindings`: `$event` per grammar, the shorthand checks, `NG8121`. `BREAKING CHANGE` for ``. 5. `feat(core): resolve styles with a style resolver`: the declarations grammar, the shorthand table, the per-property diff, `(style)` and `(attr.style)` across compiler, type checker, and runtime. `BREAKING CHANGE` for style listeners. 6. `feat(compiler-cli): add attribute resolver diagnostics`: `NG8120`, `NG8122`, and their guide pages. 7. `feat(core): resolve attributes automatically`: `withAutoResolution()` and `NG0322`. 8. `docs: add an attribute resolver guide`: the angular.dev guide page, its navigation entry, and links from the host elements, styling, `NG8120`, and `NG8122` pages.
    ## Evidence - **Before:** `
  • ` with a directive's `[attr.role]="'menuitem'"` renders `role="menuitem"`. **After:** with `(attr.role)="$event.resolve($event.resolver())"`, it renders `role="separator"`. - **Before:** `` with `host: {class: 'px-4 py-2'}` renders `class="px-4 py-2 px-2"`. **After:** with `provideAttributeResolvers({class: twMerge})` and a host `(class)`, it renders `class="py-2 px-2"`.
    Tests and cost All pass on the last commit, on `main` at `d5b60537e1`. Before that rebase, each commit passed its own targets. | Target | Specs | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | `//packages/core/test/acceptance/attribute_resolver:attribute_resolver` (Domino) | 244 | | `//packages/core/test/acceptance/attribute_resolver:attribute_resolver_web_chromium` | pass | | `//packages/core/test/acceptance/attribute_resolver:auto_resolution`, `--runs_per_test=10` | 56 | | `//packages/core/test/acceptance:acceptance` | 2725 | | `//packages/platform-server/test:test`, with the hydration specs | 433 | | `//packages/platform-server/test:attribute_resolver_auto_hydration_test`, 10 runs | 10 | | `//packages/compiler-cli/test/ngtsc:ngtsc` | 7322 | | `//packages/compiler-cli/test/ngtsc:ngtsc_ngp` | 7322, 856 pending | | `//packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/test:test` | 1477 | | `//packages/compiler/test:test`, with the type-check block specs that moved there | pass | | Compliance `full`, `linked`, `declaration-only`, `codegen`, with `r3_view_compiler_attribute_resolver` | pass | | Bundling `symbol_test`s | hook symbols only | Cost per element, measured before the last performance change (static styles parsed once, source-free elements skipped), so the refresh figures are upper bounds. JIT dev mode, Domino, N=1000, extra µs over plain Angular: | Attribute | Binding | Create | Unchanged refresh | One source changes | | --------- | -------- | -----: | ----------------: | -----------------: | | `class` | explicit | +15 | +10 | +11 | | `class` | auto | +16 | +1.7 | +11 | | `class` | auto off | +3.5 | +0.15 | +0.33 | | `role` | explicit | +3.2 | +7.0 | +4.5 | | `style` | explicit | +32 | +22 | +30 | In the measured example app, a single `(attr.role)` binding added about 7.1 kB gzip; apps that don't use the feature pay null checks in three hooks. Automatic resolution takes five `LView` slots for each enrolled name that can be resolved on an element a directive matches, unless the element already resolves that name with a binding.
    ## Merge Danger **Door:** one-way `(class)`, `(style)`, and every `(attr.x)` become reserved binding names with new public API. Removing them later breaks apps and libraries that adopt them, and partial declarations that use them require a `22.3.0` linker. **Blast Radius:** templates
    Who is affected - Templates and hosts that listen to outputs or events named `class`, `style`, or `attr.x` through those bindings change behavior; see the breaking changes below. - Apps that don't use the feature pay a null check per view refresh and per directive host at creation. - `ComponentFactory.create` reads a root host's hydration information before its directives run. That path runs for every hydrated app.
    Known limits, documented - The style resolver models a CSS subset: a shorthand table and a small tokenizer, not full CSS Syntax; importance between a shorthand and its longhands isn't modeled. - Style hydration reconciles by ownership; a server-only property from a `[style]` map key stays. - `NG8122` matches attribute names in lowercase and doesn't follow value aliases of a base class. - A template first created before a name enrolls for automatic resolution doesn't resolve it; the name registry lives for the process. - An app's own resolver receives one argument per value, so a list past the engine's argument limit throws there; built-in rules read arrays. - In production, a function passed to a scalar `resolve()` becomes its source text; dev mode throws `NG0320`. - The `ngp` backend doesn't run the resolver host checks, type checks, or extended diagnostics; those specs are on its known-failures list. - Domino doesn't escape custom-property names when it serializes styles on the server.
    ## PR Checklist - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type - [ ] Bugfix - [x] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? When several sources set one attribute on an element, the last write wins (`class` and `style` take the union). Apps can't resolve conflicts such as `px-4` and `px-2`, or keep a template's `role` over a directive's binding. Issue Number: angular/angular#67519 ## What is the new behavior? - `provideAttributeResolvers(map, ...features)` registers a resolver per attribute name for the element injectors below it; each name is looked up separately. Without one, a built-in rule applies. - `(attr.x)="handler($event)"` receives the attribute's event: the collected `sources`, the bound `resolver(...extras)`, and `resolve(value)`. `(class)` and `(style)` are shorthands that take a callback. Without a `resolve()` call, the built-in rule applies. - Every resolver binding on an element runs, from the lowest to the highest priority, and receives the previous result folded into the sources. - `withAutoResolution()` in the root providers resolves enrolled names on every element that a component or directive matches; `withAutoResolution(false)` turns it off for a subtree. - Resolvers run during server rendering and hydration, subject to the documented style reconciliation and serialization limits. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [x] Yes - [ ] No - `(class)`, `(style)`, and `(attr.)` bindings, in templates, `host` metadata, and partial declarations, no longer listen to events or outputs with those names; they resolve the attribute. With strict templates, `NG8120` warns for a same-named directive output. Migration: rename the output or event with its handler, or subscribe in code. - `@HostListener('class')`, `@HostListener('style')`, and `@HostListener('attr.')` are compile errors (`NG5001`). Migration: bind the resolver in `host`, or rename the event. - Compile errors: an `(attr.)` for a namespaced, event-handler, or sanitized attribute; a second resolver of one attribute on one element or in one `host`; a shorthand that is a chain of statements (use `(attr.class)` with `$event.resolve(...)`); a resolver on `` (`NG8121`). ## Other information A guide page, `guide/components/attribute-resolvers`, comes with the PR; the `NG8120` and `NG8122` pages come with commit 6.

Issues.Title: Hydration writes every static attribute and binding again, even when the server rendered the same value
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

During hydration, Angular reuses the DOM nodes that the server rendered, but it still writes their values again:

- `setupStaticAttributes()` writes every static attribute, the static `class`, and the static `style` of each reused element.
- On the first update after hydration, attribute, property, class, and style bindings write their values, because they have no previous value to compare with.

The values are the ones the server rendered, so the DOM ends up the same. The writes still cost time, and a `class` or `style` write makes the browser recalculate styles.

#71874 stops these writes only for attributes that make the browser load a resource again: `src` on `iframe`, `embed`, `video`, and `audio`, and `data` on `object`. This issue tracks the cost of all the other writes.

On a table with 300 rows of static classes, ARIA attributes, and SVG icons, hydration makes 12,961 attribute writes, and 12,871 of them keep the same value. I measured an experimental patch that skips a static attribute, class, or style when the DOM already has its value:

| Table, 300 rows | Today | Experimental patch |
|---|---|---|
| Attribute writes during hydration | 12,961 | 365 |
| Hydration time | 22.3 ms | 10.0 ms (−55%) |
| Hydration time, 4× CPU throttling | 162.0 ms | 61.6 ms (−62%) |
| Elements restyled after hydration | 1,247 | 45 |

Hydration time runs from `bootstrapApplication()` to `ApplicationRef.whenStable()`, in headless Chrome 156 with the cache enabled. Each value is the median of 7 page loads. #62672 reported the same writes, and the discussion there put the visible effect down to DevTools disabling the cache. The cost measured here is main-thread time, not network.

The experimental patch isn't a proposal as it stands, because of `class` and `style`. An element can combine a static class with a binding or a directive, as in `<div class="card" [class.active]="isActive">`. The server then renders `class="card active"`, which differs from the static `card`, so core writes `card` and the binding adds `active` back. A comparison doesn't remove those writes, and skipping the static value altogether breaks other cases (see #71200).

On the table, `class` accounts for 3,915 of the writes. Most of the others are static `role`, `title`, `aria-*`, `width`, and `height` attributes, which don't have that problem.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro

The experimental patch is the `core` variant in [`bench/patch.mjs` at commit `d6b35a8`](https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro/blob/d6b35a8/bench/patch.mjs). The measurements above are in [`results/timings.txt`](https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro/blob/d6b35a8/results/timings.txt) and [`results/dom-writes.txt`](https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro/blob/d6b35a8/results/dom-writes.txt) at the same commit. To run them, check out `d6b35a8`, then run `npm ci`, `npm run build:variants`, and `npm run bench`.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

No exception.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.6
Angular           : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 26.11.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.20.0
Chrome            : 156
```

### Anything else?

Related: #52477, #52478, #71200, and #71874.

Issues.Title: Global styles cannot be set for libraries
Issues.Body:

Don't known / other

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The architect.build.options.styles key is accepted for applications, allowing global styles to be set.
But the `@angular/cli/lib/config/schema.json` schema only allows it for applications and not for libraries.
That makes it impossible to follow [this tutorial](https://angular.dev/guide/animations/css#creating-reusable-animations) in libraries, to define animations to be used in components defined by the library.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add a TODO for negated arrayWithExactContents in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
`transformArrayWithExactContents` splits the assertion into a `.toHaveLength()` check and a `.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining())` check without looking for `.not`. A negated assertion is split into two negated checks, which asserts that neither condition holds instead of not both: an array with the right length but different contents passes in Jasmine and fails after the migration.

Vitest has no single matcher for exact-contents-in-any-order, so a faithful negation cannot be expressed by splitting. Leave the negated form unchanged and add a TODO comment instead, matching the existing handling of a dynamic (non-literal) argument.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): handle pending() in focused and skipped tests in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
`transformPending` only matches calls whose expression is the bare `it` identifier, but `transformFocusedAndSkippedTests` runs earlier in the pipeline and has already renamed `fit` to `it.only` and `xit` to `it.skip`. A focused test containing `pending()` is therefore migrated to `it.only` with the `pending()` call left in place, which throws a ReferenceError at runtime since Vitest has no `pending` global; a skipped test keeps a dangling `pending()` call that no longer compiles once the Jasmine types are removed.

Also match the renamed `it.only` and `it.skip` forms and convert both to `it.skip` with the usual TODO comment. A pending spec never runs its body in Jasmine, even when focused, so `it.skip` preserves the observed behavior.

Verified with two new `transformPending` cases that run the full transform pipeline on `fit` and `xit` inputs; both fail without this change and `//packages/schematics/angular:test` passes with it.

Issues.Title: `ng update` reinstalls with lifecycle scripts skipped and no notice (since 22.3.0-next.5)
Issues.Body:
### Command

update

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.2.6 (every stable release; also 22.3.0-next.4)

### Description

Since `22.3.0-next.5`, the final "Installing packages" step of `ng update` passes the package
manager's ignore-scripts flag (`npm install --ignore-scripts`; `--mode=skip-build` for modern yarn).
For npm, the update first deletes `node_modules` ("Cleaning node modules directory"), so after the
reinstall **every** dependency's `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall` script — including the
project's own root `postinstall` — has been skipped. Nothing re-runs them, nothing is printed, and
there is no flag to opt out. For pnpm/yarn/bun there is no wipe, but scripts of the packages changed
by the update are skipped the same way.

Projects that rely on lifecycle scripts break in ways that are hard to connect back to the update:

- `patch-package` via root `postinstall`: patches are silently not applied, and the migrations that
  run right after the install operate on the unpatched tree;
- `puppeteer`, `cypress`, and similar packages whose postinstall downloads a platform binary.

This comes from a69fe511c ("default ignoreScripts to true when install options are provided"). In
all released versions the final install runs scripts normally: v21.0 still used the legacy
`installAll()` (no flag), and from 21.1 through 22.2 the `= { ignoreScripts: true }` parameter
default on `install()` was replaced entirely by the options object the update command passes
(`{ ignorePeerDependencies }`), so the flag was never added. a69fe511c makes the default apply
per property, which looks right for the temporary tooling installs — but it also silently turns on
script skipping for the final, persistent install of the user's project.

If skipping scripts here is intended, could the command print a notice (e.g. "Lifecycle scripts were
skipped during installation; run your package manager's install/rebuild command to execute them")
and/or offer an opt-out? Otherwise, the final install could pass `ignoreScripts: false` to restore
the stable-release behavior.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `npx @angular/cli@22.2 new repro --defaults && cd repro`
2. Add a visible root lifecycle script to `package.json`:
   `"postinstall": "node -e \"require('node:fs').writeFileSync('postinstall-ran.txt','yes')\""`
3. `npm install` → `postinstall-ran.txt` is created. Delete it: `rm postinstall-ran.txt`
4. `npm install --save-dev --save-exact @angular/cli@22.3.0-next.5`
5. `npx ng update @angular/core --next`
6. After "Cleaning node modules directory" and "Installing packages" finish, `postinstall-ran.txt`
   does not exist — no install script ran, with no notice. Repeating steps 4–5 with
   `@angular/cli@22.3.0-next.4` in step 4 recreates the file.

### Exception or Error

```text
(none — the scripts are skipped without any notice, which is the issue)
```

### Your Environment

```text
_                      _                 ____ _     ___
    / \   _ __   __ _ _   _| | __ _ _ __     / ___| |   |_ _|
   / △ \ | '_ \ / _` | | | | |/ _` | '__|   | |   | |    | |
  / ___ \| | | | (_| | |_| | | (_| | |      | |___| |___ | |
 /_/   \_\_| |_|\__, |\__,_|_|\__,_|_|       \____|_____|___|
                |___/
    

Angular CLI       : 22.3.0-next.5
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : yarn 1.22.22
Operating System  : darwin arm64
```

### Anything else relevant?

Code on `main`:

- `packages/angular/cli/src/commands/update/cli.ts:568-602` — the npm-only "Cleaning node modules
  directory" task followed by `packageManager.install({ ignorePeerDependencies })`, with no
  `ignoreScripts` override;
- `packages/angular/cli/src/package-managers/package-manager.ts:397` —
  `const { force, ignoreScripts = true, ignorePeerDependencies } = options;` in `install()`.

Defaulting to ignore-scripts for the temporary package acquisitions (`ng add`/`ng update` tooling
installs) is good hardening and not what this issue is about — only the final project install.
Reproduces with every package manager; npm is affected most because of the preceding `node_modules`
wipe. Not OS- or browser-specific.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): pass an explicit port of 0 through to the dev server
Issues.Body:
Previously, requesting an ephemeral port (`--port 0`) was resolved by binding a throwaway net.Server to learn the real port before handing that concrete number to Vite or webpack-dev-server, which then bound it again. This avoided a Vite bug where `server.port: 0` was ignored and the default port (5173) was used instead.

That bug is fixed upstream (vitejs/vite#7529, vitejs/vite#23158), and webpack-dev-server has always bound port 0 correctly via Node's own http.Server. Pass 0 straight through instead of pre-resolving it, removing the redundant double-bind.

Verified via the existing port_spec.ts "random free port" test for both the Vite-based and webpack-based dev server, which covers this exact scenario.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): preserve stub-by-default semantics for create Spy with an original function
Issues.Body:
`jasmine.createSpy(name, originalFn)` stores the original function but does not invoke it: the default spy plan is a no-op stub, and the original function only runs after `.and.callThrough()`. The refactor-jasmine-vitest schematic maps this call to `vi.fn(originalFn)`, which invokes the function immediately, so a migrated bare spy suddenly calls through and can change test behavior.

Append `.mockReturnValue(undefined)` when `createSpy` is given an original function and is not chained with an `.and` strategy. This keeps the original function available for `mockReset()` while preserving the stub-by-default behavior, mirroring how bare `spyOn` calls are already handled. Chained spies are unchanged: `.and.callThrough()` keeps mapping to a plain `vi.fn(originalFn)` and strategies such as `.and.returnValue()` keep replacing the stub.

The updated spec fails without the fix: `jasmine.createSpy('mySpy', () => 'foo')` was migrated to `vi.fn(() => 'foo').mockName('mySpy')`, which calls the function.

Issues.Title: `ng generate application` produces a missing stylesheet when a workspace component type is configured
Issues.Body:
Hi Angular team! 

I found a case where a newly generated application fails to build when the workspace has a default component `type` configured.

### Command

generate, build

### Description

With `"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }` in the workspace-level `schematics` section of `angular.json`, generating an application with the 2025 file naming style produces `app.component.css`, but the generated `app.ts` references `./app.css`.

As a result, the application fails its first build with NG2008. Both `app.ts` and an extra `app.component.ts` are generated.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Create a workspace:

   ```sh
   ng new component-type-repro --create-application=false --defaults --package-manager=npm --skip-git
   cd component-type-repro
   ```

2. Add the following at the **top level** of `angular.json` (alongside `projects`):

   ```json
   "schematics": {
     "@schematics/angular:component": {
       "type": "component"
     }
   }
   ```

3. Generate and build an application:

   ```sh
   ng generate application demo --file-name-style-guide=2025 --style=css --ssr=false --skip-install
   ng build demo --configuration=development
   ```

**Actual behavior**

The generated files include:

```text
projects/demo/src/app/app.ts
projects/demo/src/app/app.component.ts
projects/demo/src/app/app.component.css
```

There is no `app.css`, but `app.ts` contains:

```ts
styleUrl: './app.css',
```

**Expected behavior**

The root component files and their references should consistently follow the selected application naming style: `app.ts`, `app.html`, and `app.css` for 2025. The generated application should build successfully.

The workspace component default should still apply when generating ordinary components separately.

### Exception or Error

```text
✘ [ERROR] NG2008: Could not find stylesheet file './app.css'. [plugin angular-compiler]

    projects/demo/src/app/app.ts:7:12:
      7 │   styleUrl: './app.css',
        ╵             ~~~~~~~~~~~
```

### Your Environment

Reproduced with the locally built CLI from `main` at d5035923f0e357b2526c98110125eee04b05192f, using the repository's Bazel E2E runner. Its `ng version` output reports:

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0-next.5
Angular           : 22.3.0-next.4
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 12.0.2
Operating System  : darwin x64
```

I have not established the last working version.

### Anything else relevant?

- #31053 introduced the file naming style option and describes the 2025 root component filename as `app.ts`.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/pwa): add the manifest link when the index option is an object
Issues.Body:
The application and browser builders accept the `index` option either as a string or as an `{ input, output }` object. `ng add @angular/pwa` only collects string values when looking for index files to update, so a project using the object form gets no `<link rel="manifest">` tag. The failure is silent: when the object points at a custom file such as `src/app-index.html`, no index file is updated at all, and the installed application never loads the web app manifest.

Collect the `input` path of an object-form `index` alongside the string form, for both the target options and each configuration.

The new spec fails without the fix: with
`"index": { "input": "projects/bar/src/app-index.html", "output": "index.html" }`, the schematic left `app-index.html` without the manifest link.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add the missing vi import for toHaveBeenCalledBefore in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
The `toHaveBeenCalledBefore` transformation rewrites the matcher to a comparison of `vi.mocked(spy).mock.invocationCallOrder` values but never registers `vi` as a pending value import. When the schematic runs with `--add-imports`, the migrated file only imports `expect` and fails to compile with "Cannot find name 'vi'" unless another transformation in the same file happens to use `vi`.

Register the `vi` import when the matcher is transformed, as every other transformation that emits `vi.*` already does.

The new spec fails without the fix: the migrated output contained `import { expect } from 'vitest'` instead of `import { expect, vi } from 'vitest'`.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jsdom/jsdom (jsdom)</summary>

### [`v31.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/releases/tag/v31.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/compare/v30.1.3...v31.0.0)

##### Breaking changes

- Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from `canvas` to `@napi-rs/canvas`. Install `@napi-rs/canvas` v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing `canvas` alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the [canvas migration guidance](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/blob/v31.0.0/README.md#canvas-support). Added WebP serialization through `canvas.toDataURL()` and `canvas.toBlob()`. Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing `load`, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. Fixed canvas context and serialization behavior, including unsupported context types, read-only `ctx.canvas`, image-drawing exceptions, MIME type and quality normalization, and asynchronous `null` results from `canvas.toBlob()` for empty canvases or encoding failures. ([@​Brooooooklyn](https://redirect.github.com/Brooooooklyn))
- Changed CSS parsing, selector matching, and computed styles to use a new integrated implementation, with substantially expanded support and faster selector queries and repeated style reads. This includes cascade layers, nesting, `@scope`, custom-property substitution and registration through `@property` and `CSS.registerProperty()`, typed `attr()`, conditional `if()`, shadow-tree styling with `:host`, `::slotted()`, and `::part()`, pseudo-element computed styles, and constructable stylesheets with `document.adoptedStyleSheets` and `shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets`. Fixed numerous cascade, shorthand, serialization, and default-style issues; computed declarations now stay live across DOM and stylesheet changes. CSS serialization and computed values can differ from previous releases.
- Changed HTML and XML parsing to pause at blocking scripts until their required resources are ready. The `JSDOM` constructor, `JSDOM.fromURL()`, and `JSDOM.fromFile()` can now return partially parsed documents. Wait for `DOMContentLoaded` for the finished tree, or the window's `load` event for load-delaying resources, checking `document.readyState` first in case the event has already fired. XML syntax errors encountered after asynchronous parsing resumes are reported through the virtual console as `"xml-parsing"` errors.

##### Other changes

- Added `window.reportError()`, which dispatches an `error` event and reports uncanceled errors to the virtual console. ([@​sarankumar1325](https://redirect.github.com/sarankumar1325))
- Added `element.ariaBrailleLabel` and `element.ariaBrailleRoleDescription`. ([@​Kjubikstronk](https://redirect.github.com/Kjubikstronk))
- Fixed page-completion `load` events to fire only on the window. Use `window.addEventListener("load", ...)` or `window.onload` instead of listening on the document.
- Fixed `document.open()`, including implicit calls from `document.write()`, to clear event listeners and handlers from the document, its descendants, and its window when replacing the input stream.
- Fixed `document.write()` to process successive writes through the parser's input stream, preserve insertion points across nested scripts, and make completed text immediately visible. Script-created input streams now remain open until `document.close()`.
- Fixed dynamically inserted scripts to respect `script.async = false` execution order, use their source text and document from preparation time, and avoid executing after adoption into another document. Scripts parsed through inert fragment APIs no longer execute when subsequently inserted.
- Fixed unrelated images, stylesheets, and frames being delayed behind scripts, and resource completion events firing before nested stylesheet imports finish. Cyclic imports no longer prevent completion, and `<style>` elements in shadow trees now fire `load` events.
- Fixed `window.stop()` to cancel pending subresource and `XMLHttpRequest` requests in descendant frames and suppress completion events for canceled loads, while allowing subsequent requests to proceed.
- Fixed repeated `document.close()` calls replaying readiness and load events, and incorrect iframe load events when reopening documents from event handlers.
- Fixed memory leaks where pending request interceptor promises retained closed windows, introduced in v28.0.0.
- Fixed focus remaining on elements that become non-focusable after DOM or style changes. Focus now moves asynchronously to the document's viewport, and `element.blur()` can release it immediately.
- Fixed `document.hasFocus()` returning false before an element is focused or during focus transitions within the document, including inside frames.
- Fixed `<template>` parsing and `template.innerHTML` serialization in XML documents, including templates with namespace prefixes. ([@​b84330808](https://redirect.github.com/b84330808))
- Fixed `rect.toJSON()` and `performance.toJSON()` to create their result objects in the method's realm instead of the host Node.js realm.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): use the workspace package manager in catalog update guidance
Issues.Body:
When `ng update` aborts because a package uses the `catalog:` protocol, the manual migration steps hardcode pnpm and yarn: the install step suggests 'pnpm install' for every package manager except yarn, and the catalog file hint only names pnpm-workspace.yaml and .yarnrc.yml. Bun workspaces also support catalogs, so a bun workspace is told to run 'pnpm install' and to look for files it does not have.

Build the install command from the detected package manager and name the catalog location it actually uses: pnpm-workspace.yaml for pnpm, .yarnrc.yml for yarn, and the 'workspaces.catalog' field in the root package.json for bun. The previous generic text is kept as a fallback when the package manager is unknown.

The new spec fails without the fix: with `packageManager: 'bun'`, the guidance suggested 'pnpm install' and the pnpm/yarn file names.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve component initialization in Karma test bundles
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not applicable: internal Karma bundling fix; no new options or public API)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Fixes #34250.

With `@angular/build:karma`, a component imported through a barrel can be captured as `undefined` in another component's `imports` array. This depends on the combination of spec entry points: an async spec importing the component directly can cause lazy module initialization to cross shared-chunk boundaries. The consuming decorator can run before the component is initialized.

The regression fixture includes:

1. A standalone layout component re-exported by a barrel.
2. A dialog importing that barrel and used by two specs.
3. A page importing the barrel and used by another spec.
4. An async spec importing the layout directly.

Against main (`2c6e8b970`), the browser reports **2 failed, 2 successful**. Both dialog specs throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ɵcmp')`.

## What is the new behavior?

The Karma build routes the discovered spec entry points through a shared virtual module that imports all selected specs. This keeps spec initialization in one module graph, avoiding the problematic partitioning across independent spec entry points.

- Preserve the existing `spec-*` entry names, including basename-collision handling.
- Keep code splitting enabled so Angular and its testing environment remain shared with the setup entry point.
- Include the original spec files as TypeScript root files, since the build entry points now refer to the virtual module.
- Preserve `include`/`exclude` selection: the virtual module only imports the specs collected by the existing discovery logic.

The same four browser specs now all pass. The added integration test exercises real Karma/Chrome execution rather than only checking generated bundle text.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Simply setting `disableCodeSplitting: true`, as suggested by the earlier Vitest fix in #33729, was insufficient for Karma in this reproduction: it produced testing-environment initialization errors. This change retains shared framework chunks instead.

Validation on macOS arm64, Node.js 24.22.2, pnpm 12.16.1, and Chrome Headless 159:

- `pnpm bazel test //packages/angular/build:karma_integration_tests --config=no-sharding --test_output=errors`: **42 integration specs, 0 failures**.
- ESLint for the changed implementation passes. The repository ESLint configuration excludes builder integration fixtures.
- Prettier checks for both changed files and `git diff --check` pass.

The full repository and E2E suites were not run. Large-suite build size/performance and dynamic addition of spec files during watch mode were not separately benchmarked or validated.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve unaffected localized chunk URLs
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the [guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines)
- [x] Regression tests were added to the existing i18n suites
- [ ] Docs were updated (no public option changes)

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

The application builder adds a digest of the translation files to every JavaScript bundle. Editing one locale can give unrelated chunks new URLs in every locale, forcing browsers to download them again.

Fixes #30675.

## What is the new behavior?

For one-shot browser builds with bundle hashing enabled, compute names after localization. A changed bundle gets a new URL, and bundles that reference it get updated URLs. Unchanged bundles retain their URLs. The dependency graph comes from the esbuild/Rolldown output metadata; JavaScript is parsed when references need to be rewritten or to find worker URLs that are absent from the graph.

Watch, server builds, and builds with custom code plugins keep the existing hashing path.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Measurements and verification

**Chromium 153, warm browser cache.** Changed one French XLF message used by a lazy chunk, switched deployments on the same origin, and opened the page and one independent lazy chunk. JS used immutable cache headers; HTML used `no-store`. All three runs per locale and variant gave the same results. Bytes are Brotli response bodies, excluding headers.

| Locale | JS responses (main → PR) | JS bytes downloaded (main → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| French, translation changed | 5 → 2 | 36,822 → 34,974 (−5.0%) |
| German, translation unchanged | 5 → 0 | 36,596 → 0 |

**Build time.** Synthetic Angular app with 240 lazy routes, three locales and 254 JS outputs per locale. Five alternating pairs per mode, after a warm-up pair; CLI disk cache disabled. The full build compares this PR with upstream `main`. The rehash stage compares the metadata approach with the initial implementation that parsed JavaScript to build the graph.

| Source maps | Full build, median paired delta vs. `main` (range) | Rehash stage, initial implementation → metadata |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Off | +30 ms (−128 to +308 ms) | 370 → 77 ms |
| On | +138 ms (−106 to +298 ms) | 404 → 124 ms |

The stage timings are separate instrumented runs, including graph construction. These figures describe the test fixtures, not production CDN traffic or general build performance.

**Validation.** Ran 50 i18n tests and the localized-hashes e2e scenario locally, including sourcemap references and SHA-384 integrity for the emitted entry bundle. Checked localized workers in Chromium with esbuild and Rolldown. The initial `--watch` build and two rebuilds after editing a lazy TypeScript module produced identical filenames and SHA-256 digests for the entry bundle, lazy chunk and HTML on `main` and the PR branch. Each rebuild updated the import and removed the old chunk.

Issues.Title: Debug ID changes the bytes of polyfills and main but not their file names, so cached files fail the SRI check
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

Yes. It started with the debug IDs in 22.1.0.

### Description

Follow-up to #34574.

The builder names `polyfills-<hash>.js` and `main-<hash>.js` first. Then it adds a `//# debugId=<id>` line to the file. It computes `<id>` from the source map after it rewrites the map to add `x_google_ignoreList`. The file name does not cover that line.

So when a builder release writes the source map differently, the JS bytes change and the file name stays the same. 22.1.8 did that. Commit 5a0d226b7c moved `x_google_ignoreList` to the start of the map.

With `subresourceIntegrity`, the new `index.html` pins the new bytes. A CDN or browser cache that kept the old file under the same URL serves the old bytes, and the browser blocks the script. This happened to us in production with `polyfills-<hash>.js`.

#34583 fixed this for the chunks of the chunk optimizer. It does not cover files that esbuild names, such as `main` and `polyfills`. 22.2.6 still computes their debug ID from the rewritten map.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.1.8 new repro --defaults --ssr=false
cd repro
npm install zone.js
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.6
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.options.polyfills '["zone.js"]'
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.sourceMap true
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.subresourceIntegrity true
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.6
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.8
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.8
```

Both builds write `polyfills-QWJLBG44.js` and `main-HHND32NM.js`. In each file, only the `//# debugId=` line differs:

```
polyfills-QWJLBG44.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=d932f97d-b667-5462-b3b7-b328a1ce7f5a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=81c8766a-7d41-50fd-ac6d-16c3c4ed6358
main-HHND32NM.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=e3a30145-1442-57c2-96a7-a88f9bf43b0a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=50dd2d3c-f1e3-5224-9587-43f24f562421
```

The two `index.html` files pin different hashes for the same URLs. For both files, the two source maps have the same content in a different key order.

### Exception or Error

```
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://example.com/polyfills-JTOAPWZJ.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '...'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI: 22.1.8
@angular/build: 22.1.6, then 22.1.8
@angular/core: 22.2.5
zone.js: 0.16.3
Node: 24.17.0
OS: macOS
```

### Anything else relevant?

Expected: when the bytes of a hashed file change, its name changes too.

A possible fix is to compute the debug ID from the JS before the builder adds the debug ID line, not from the rewritten map. The file name already covers the JS.

Issues.Title: fix(material/slider): align slider thumb with cursor on Firefox during drag
Issues.Body:
#### Description
On Firefox, when clicking and dragging the slider thumb, the visual thumb was pulled closer to the center of the track than the cursor, especially visible near the ends of the slider track.

This occurred because `.mdc-slider__input` did not reset native range appearance or pseudo-elements (`::-moz-range-thumb` and `::-moz-range-track`). In Gecko's user-agent stylesheet, the native range thumb has a default width of `1.4em` (~22.4px) with border insets, whereas Angular's geometry calculation assumes a 16px knob diameter (`_knobRadius: 8`). This resulted in a dead-zone where Firefox's native drag coordinates lagged behind the mouse position.

This PR:
- Resets native appearance (`appearance: none`, `-moz-appearance: none`, `-webkit-appearance: none`) and clears background on `.mdc-slider__input`.
- Explicitly sizes `::-moz-range-thumb` to 16px to match `_knobRadius` and clears borders on `::-moz-range-track`.
- Adds unit test coverage asserting native appearance reset on the input element.

Fixes #34094

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): use latest trigger data when menu is reopened
Issues.Body: Fixes #26256 `CdkMenuTriggerBase.getMenuContentPortal()` only creates a new `TemplatePortal` when `menuTemplateRef` changes. The portal captures `menuData` as its context when it's created, so changes to `cdkMenuTriggerData` / `cdkContextMenuTriggerData` were never picked up. The menu kept rendering with the data from the first time it was opened. This also compares `menuData` against the portal's context and recreates the portal when it's a different object. The portal is only read when the menu opens, so an already open menu doesn't change; the new data shows up the next time it's opened. That matches what the issue asks for. Mutating the same object in place keeps working as it does today, since the context is the same reference. ### Tests Added a "reopen with new data" spec for both `CdkMenuTrigger` and `CdkContextMenuTrigger`: open with `{message: 'Hello!'}`, close, switch to `{message: 'Goodbye!'}`, reopen. ``` bazel test //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` Without the change in `menu-trigger-base.ts` both new specs fail with `Expected 'Hello!' to be 'Goodbye!'.` ### Manual check Same setup as the issue's StackBlitz: `[cdkMenuTriggerData]="{counter: counter()}"`, open the menu, close it, click "Increment" twice, open it again (Chromium, CDK 22.2.6 and then the same build with this change): Before: the button says 2, the menu still says 0 After: the menu says 2

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): ngMenuContent is never destroyed once the trigger has been focused, ignoring preserveContent
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`ngMenu` hosts `DeferredContentAware` and exposes its `preserveContent` input, which defaults to `false`. So `ngMenuContent` should behave like `ngTabContent` and `ngAccordionContent`: rendered while the panel is visible, and destroyed when it hides.

It isn't. The menu computes the content's visibility as:

```ts
contentVisible = this._pattern.visible() || !!this.parent()?._pattern.hasBeenInteracted()
```

`hasBeenInteracted` is set to `true` in `onFocusIn` / `onKeydown` of `MenuTriggerPattern`, `MenuItemPattern`, `MenuPattern` and `MenuBarPattern`, and nothing ever sets it back to `false`. That has two effects:

1. **Content is built before the menu opens.** Tabbing onto the trigger (or onto a submenu's parent item) renders the deferred rows, even if the menu is never opened.
2. **Content is never destroyed afterwards.** Once the parent has been focused, `contentVisible` is `true` for the rest of the component's life, so `preserveContent: false` has no effect, through close, Escape, outside click and item selection alike.

For comparison, tabs and accordion set `contentVisible.set(this.visible())`, and their content is torn down when hidden.

Rendering a submenu's rows when its parent item gains focus looks intentional: it lets one ArrowRight move focus straight into the submenu. The problem is that the flag is sticky. Something like "parent is focused or active right now" would keep that benefit and still allow teardown.

**Why it matters:** the main reason to defer menu content is a menu repeated per row of a table or list. With the current behaviour, every menu the user has focused, even without opening it, keeps its rows for the life of the page, and `preserveContent` can't opt out of that.

### Reproduction

Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section **C**, with section **D** as the tabs control)

Issues.Title: bug(cdk/scrolling): nested viewports and overlay content inherit the outer `scrollWindow` / `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` scroller
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description

`scrollWindow` and `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` provide `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` through `providers`, and `CdkVirtualScrollViewport` takes it with `inject(VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, {optional: true})`. So every viewport below them in the injector tree uses the outer scroller, not just the viewport it was meant for:

- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` nested in the rows of an outer virtual list that uses `scrollWindow` or `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`;
- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` inside an overlay opened from such a row (`cdkConnectedOverlay`, and therefore also a virtual list inside a `mat-select` panel), even though the overlay isn't inside the scrolling element in the DOM at all.

Such an inner viewport never gets the `cdk-virtual-scrollable` class, so it can't scroll by itself. The mouse wheel scrolls the page or the outer element instead, the rendered range follows the outer scroller, and the rendered items spill out of the viewport box over the following rows.

The docs describe both options per viewport ("add the `scrollWindow` attribute to the `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport`"), and nothing says nested viewports inherit the scroller. As a workaround, `{provide: VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, useValue: null}` on a component between the two viewports makes the inner one scroll by itself again.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/7ytfjjia-a8v2qj79

It's the docs example "Virtual scrolling window" opened via "Edit in StackBlitz", with only the example file replaced.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open the StackBlitz. The outer list uses `scrollWindow`, and every row has its own 150px high virtual list with 100 items. The red line under each inner list already says it uses the outer scroller.
2. Hover an inner list and scroll with the mouse wheel: the page scrolls, the list doesn't.
3. The radio buttons at the top switch the outer list to `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` and move the inner list into a `cdkConnectedOverlay`. All four combinations are broken.
4. Select "its own viewport" to compare: the inner lists scroll by themselves.

### Expected Behavior

A viewport nested inside another virtual scroll viewport, or rendered in an overlay, scrolls by itself, the same way it does when the outer list uses its own viewport.

### Actual Behavior

The inner viewport uses the outer scroller (`viewport.scrollable !== viewport`) in all four combinations:

- `scrollWindow`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the page, the inner list renders ~40 items that overflow its 150px box and follow the page scroll.
- `scrollWindow`, in an overlay: the wheel scrolls the page instead of the list.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the outer element.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, in an overlay: the list can't be scrolled at all and stays on its first 30 items, which overflow the panel.

With an outer list that scrolls itself, both placements work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.5
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (same with 22.3.0-next.5)
- Browser(s): Chrome 157
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS 26

---

Not a regression: the scroller has been injected this way since `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` was added in #24394 (14.1.0). A possible direction: a viewport could act as a boundary for its content, so viewports and overlays declared inside it don't inherit an outer scrollable, and `scrollWindow` could apply only to its own host viewport.

We ran into this with Taiga UI dropdowns that use a virtual scroll inside virtualized lists (taiga-family/taiga-ui#10095).

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): don't close menu until outside press is released
Issues.Body: Fixes #27878 With a standalone `cdkMenuTriggerFor`, pressing down anywhere outside the open menu closes it immediately, before the button is released. As noted in the issue, the outside click listener never gets a chance: the mousedown blurs the menu, `menuStack.hasFocus` emits `false` and `CdkMenuTrigger` calls `closeAll()`. That means the close can't be cancelled by moving the pointer away before releasing (WCAG 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation), and it's different from the menu bar and `mat-menu`. I didn't remove the `hasFocus` listener, because it's also what closes the menu when focus leaves it from the keyboard (Tab, or focus moving somewhere else programmatically). Instead, while a root menu is open the trigger now tracks pointer presses on the document: - `pointerdown` outside of the trigger and the menu stack marks that a press is in progress. - If focus leaves the menu during that press, closing is deferred until `pointerup`. - On `pointerup` the menu closes if the pointer was released outside, and stays open if it was moved back onto the menu. - `pointercancel` and closing the menu reset the state, and the listeners are only attached while the menu is open. I listen on the document rather than relying on the overlay's outside click events. A press on the empty area below a short page lands on ``, which the outside click dispatcher (attached to `body`) doesn't see, and the menu would stay open after the release. Focus loss that isn't caused by a press closes the menu right away, the same as before. ### Tests New specs in `menu-trigger.spec.ts` (standalone trigger): - focus leaving the menu without a press still closes it - press outside → focus leaves → menu stays open → `pointerup` outside closes it - press outside → focus leaves → `pointerup` on the menu keeps it open - a press that was already released doesn't stop focus loss from closing the menu ``` bazel test //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` Without the change in `menu-trigger.ts`, the two press specs fail (`Expected 1 to be 2.`). ### Manual check Standalone trigger + `cdkMenu` with a nested submenu, CDK 22.2.6 and then the same build with this change. I drove it with Playwright using real mouse events, holding the button for 500ms on the page background: | | Chromium 156 | Firefox 157 | WebKit 27.2 | |---|---|---|---| | menu open while the press is held (before → after) | no → yes | no → yes | no → yes | | closed after releasing outside | yes → yes | yes → yes | yes → yes | | press outside, drag back onto the menu, release | closed → stays open | closed → stays open | closed → stays open | | Tab out of the menu | closes → closes | closes → closes | closes → closes | Before, while the mouse button is still held down outside the menu: After:

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): activate interactive content inside menu items
Issues.Body:
### What does this PR do?

Menu items can wrap native interactive elements (a link, a button, an input), but
`Enter`/`Space` only ran the menu's selection logic. The wrapped element was never
activated, so link items and items with `(click)` handlers inside the content were
effectively mouse-only.

`MenuItemPattern` now resolves the interactive element rendered inside the item and
clicks it when the item is triggered. The click bubbles up to the menu's existing
`click` handler, so the item is still selected exactly as it is on a mouse click —
keyboard and mouse now behave the same. Items without interactive content keep their
current behavior, and menu bar items still open their submenu first.

Fixes #34072.

### Testing

- Added unit coverage in `src/aria/menu/menu.spec.ts` for a menu whose items wrap a
  link, a button, and no interactive content at all, asserting that `Enter` and
  `Space` activate the inner element and still report the selection.
- Type checking of the changed sources (`src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts` and
  `src/aria/menu/menu.spec.ts`) passes.
- Note: `bazel test //src/aria/menu:unit_tests` could not be run on my machine because
  Bazel fails to resolve the `rules_sass` toolchain on Windows, unrelated to this change.

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): activate the item element on enter and space
Issues.Body: Fixes #34072 The menu's keyboard manager prevents the default action for Enter and Space, and `MenuPattern.trigger()` only called `submit()`. So with the keyboard the item's element was never activated: `` didn't navigate and a `(click)` listener on the item didn't run. Both work with the mouse because the real click happens before the menu handles it. `trigger()` now calls `element.click()` on the active item (when it's enabled and doesn't open a submenu) and then submits, which is the same order a pointer click goes through. The synthetic click bubbles up to the menu's `(click)` host listener, so `onClick` ignores clicks while the item is being activated. Otherwise the item would be submitted twice and focus would jump back into the menu. Items with a submenu still just open the submenu, and disabled items still do nothing. ### Tests - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Enter/Space clicks the element. A click that reaches `onClick` doesn't select twice. Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): close only the focused submenu on escape
Issues.Body: Fixes #34071 Escape inside a nested `ngMenu` was calling `closeAll()`, so the whole menu tree closed and focus jumped back to the trigger. The APG menu pattern says Escape should close the menu that has focus and put focus back on whatever opened it, and that's also how `cdk/menu` and `mat-menu` already behave. I added a `closeCurrent()` on `MenuPattern` and pointed the Escape binding at it. If the menu is a nested submenu (its parent item isn't in a menubar), it closes just that submenu with `refocus: true`, the same path ArrowLeft/`collapse()` already uses. Otherwise it falls back to `closeAll()`, so first-level menus under a trigger or a menubar close exactly as before. ### Tests New specs: - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Escape from a trigger's submenu, and from a nested submenu under a menubar menu - `menu/menu.spec.ts`: directive test using the existing Berries submenu. Escape from Blueberry leaves the main menu open and focuses Berries ``` bazel test //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` I also checked that the new tests fail without the change to `menu.ts` (all three fail with `Expected false to be true.`). ### Manual check I used the repro from the issue (https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro, section A): open menu A, go to Categorize, ArrowRight into the submenu, press Escape. The focused element is outlined in red. Before (22.2.6): both menus close and focus goes back to "Open menu A" After (same build with this change applied): the submenu closes, the root menu stays open and focus is on "Categorize" Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/ (Escape: "Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened.")
